subtitle: Lesson 14 · Enterprise Cloud Architecture & Advanced Capstone

code:
RTO  Recovery Time Objective
     "How long can this be down?"
     -> drives standby capacity

RPO  Recovery Point Objective
     "How much data can we lose?"
     -> drives backup/replication frequency
caption: A tight RTO and a loose RPO can coexist on the same system — they measure different things.

steps.label: RPO = 24 hours
steps.sub: a nightly backup job is genuinely sufficient

steps.label: RPO = 1 hour
steps.sub: needs hourly incremental backups or log shipping

steps.label: RPO = seconds
steps.sub: only continuous, often synchronous, replication qualifies

steps.label: RTO = days
steps.sub: rebuild from IaC and restore from backup — cheapest option

steps.label: RTO = under an hour
steps.sub: warm standby, running reduced, scaled up on failover

steps.label: RTO = minutes or less
steps.sub: hot standby, already at full capacity, paid for the whole time

code:
# wrong order:
#   pick "active-active" because it sounds resilient
#   then discover what it costs
#
# right order:
#   business sets RTO + RPO per workload tier
#   architecture is whatever actually meets those numbers
#   cost is the explicit tradeoff, not a surprise
caption: RTO and RPO are business decisions first — the pattern is just whatever satisfies them.

subtitle: The two patterns that implement whatever RTO and RPO actually demand.
